name: LMR10510XMFX_NOPB
title: LMR10510: 1 A step-down regulator, 3 V to 5.5 V in, 1.6 MHz or 3 MHz, SOT-23 and WSON
summary: A non-synchronous buck converter with a 130 mΩ PMOS switch on chip, needing an external Schottky catch diode. It runs from 3 V to 5.5 V, sets outputs from 0.6 V to 4.5 V through a resistor divider, and delivers up to 1 A. Current-mode control is compensated internally, and it switches at a fixed 1.6 MHz (X option) or 3 MHz (Y option). Soft start, cycle-by-cycle current limit, output overvoltage protection, undervoltage lockout and thermal shutdown are built in; shutdown current is 30 nA typical. It comes in a 5-pin SOT-23 and a 6-pin 3 mm × 3 mm WSON with exposed pad.

notes: The letter after LMR10510 sets the switching frequency: X is 1.6 MHz, Y is 3 MHz. MF is the 5-pin SOT-23 (DBV) and SD the 6-pin WSON (NGG); the WSON comes only as the Y option. A trailing E or X before /NOPB marks a 250-piece or larger reel.

circuits.title: Typical application, 1.8 V output
circuits.description: A 1.8 V buck converter using the WSON pinout. Both supply pins share the input rail with two input capacitors; R3 pulls EN up to the input, and EN is also brought out. The switch node feeds L1 and the Schottky catch diode D1. R1 and R2 divide the output down to the 0.6 V feedback level. Two output capacitors filter VOUT, and a 22 nF capacitor across the output is optional.

parts.note: 3.3 µH for the X (1.6 MHz) version

notes: U1 pins: 6 EN, 4 and 5 VINA/VIND, 2 GND, 3 SW, 1 FB.

circuits.title: LMR10510X (1.6 MHz): VIN = 5 V, VOUT = 1.2 V at 1 A
circuits.description: A 1.6 MHz buck from a 5 V rail to 1.2 V at up to 1 A. R3 holds EN at the input so the part runs whenever power is present. Equal 15 k resistors halve the output to the 0.6 V reference. D1 carries the inductor current while the switch is off; C1 and C2 are the input and output capacitors.

circuits.title: LMR10510X (1.6 MHz): VIN = 5 V, VOUT = 3.3 V at 1 A
circuits.description: A 1.6 MHz buck from a 5 V rail to 3.3 V at up to 1 A, with EN pulled to the input through R3, a 2.2 µH inductor, a Schottky catch diode and 22 µF ceramic capacitors at input and output. R1 and R2 set the output against the 0.6 V reference.
notes: Misprint: R2 should read 10k for 3.3 V (0.6 V × (1 + 45.3k / 10k) = 3.32 V); with R2 = 100k the divider sets 0.87 V.

circuits.title: LMR10510Y (3 MHz): VIN = 5 V, VOUT = 3.3 V at 1 A
circuits.description: The 3 MHz option converting 5 V to 3.3 V at up to 1 A. The higher frequency allows a 1.6 µH inductor; the rest matches the 1.6 MHz design: EN pulled to the input, Schottky catch diode, 22 µF at input and output, and a divider from the output to FB.
notes: Misprint: R2 should read 10k for 3.3 V (0.6 V × (1 + 45.3k / 10k) = 3.32 V); with R2 = 100k the divider sets 0.87 V.

circuits.title: LMR10510Y (3 MHz): VIN = 5 V, VOUT = 1.2 V at 1 A
circuits.description: The 3 MHz option converting 5 V to 1.2 V at up to 1 A, with a 1.6 µH inductor. Two equal 10 k resistors put half the output on FB, which settles at 0.6 V. EN is tied high through R3; D1 is the freewheeling Schottky.

operation.text: Fixed-frequency, current-mode PWM buck with a high-side PMOS switch. Each cycle starts when the oscillator's reset pulse falls and the switch turns on; SW rises to about VIN and the inductor current ramps up. A sense amplifier measures switch current; that signal plus a slope-compensation ramp is compared with the error amplifier output (FB against VREF). When the comparator trips, the switch stays off for the rest of the period, and the inductor current flows through the external Schottky diode, pulling SW below ground by the diode drop. Compensation is internal.
At start-up the error amplifier's reference rises from 0 V to 0.6 V over roughly 600 µs, so the output climbs at a controlled rate and inrush current is held down.
When FB rises 15 % above VREF the PMOS switch is held off, letting the output fall back toward regulation.

The part stays off until VIN exceeds 2.73 V typical and keeps running down to 2.3 V typical. About 430 mV of hysteresis stops a supply that rises non-monotonically at start-up from shutting the regulator down again.
Switch current is limited cycle by cycle: if it passes 1.75 A typical, the switch turns off for the remainder of that cycle.
Switching stops when the junction reaches 165 °C and resumes once it has cooled to about 150 °C.
EN high runs the regulator, EN low shuts it down; shutdown supply current is 30 nA typical. EN must be driven or pulled, never floating, and must not exceed the supply by more than 0.3 V.

The inductor must not saturate at the peak current of the maximum load; because the current limit acts quickly, it need not be rated at the 1.75 A typical limit (for 1 A out with 1.25 A peak, a saturation rating above 1.25 A is enough). Ferrite cores keep core loss low at these frequencies, and lower DC resistance improves efficiency.

22 µF of input capacitance is recommended. Check its voltage rating, capacitance at the working voltage and temperature, RMS current rating and ESL. Surface-mount parts are strongly preferred, since a leaded capacitor's ESL can be too high at these frequencies. POSCAP, tantalum, niobium, SP and X5R or X7R MLCCs are all suitable for input and output.

Chosen for ripple and transient response; it supplies the first part of a load step. With MLCCs the ESR is so low that the capacitive term sets the ripple, which is then close to a sine wave lagging the switching by 90°. Ceramics also shunt switching-edge noise coupled through the inductor, which tantalum does not. Together with one other external part it sets loop stability; most designs need at least 22 µF, and more usually does not harm stability. X5R or X7R types are recommended.

Use a Schottky type: it switches fast and drops little voltage. Its current rating must exceed IOUT × (1 - D) and its reverse rating must exceed the maximum input voltage with margin. The diode's conduction loss is often the largest single loss in the converter.

Put the input capacitor's and D1's ground ends close together and take them to the ground plane with at least two vias, with both parts as near the IC as possible. The output capacitor's ground goes next, near those of CIN and D1. On a two-layer board keep the bottom layer a solid ground plane except under the switch node. Keep the FB trace short since FB is high impedance; place the feedback resistors near the IC, the lower one's ground near the IC's ground, and route the VOUT sense trace away from the inductor and other switching traces. VIN, SW and VOUT carry large AC currents and should be short and wide, though wider copper radiates more; a shielded inductor reduces radiated noise.

Board size, copper weight, layer count and thermal vias all change RθJA. With the WSON, 4 to 6 vias from the exposed pad down to the ground plane are advised, and the land can be extended in a dog-bone shape with a larger ground area to lower RθJA further. The exposed pad is joined to the die attach paddle inside the package; the pins are separate exposed contacts.
